# Incident Report — NetSupport RAT Infection
**Case reference:** MTA 2024-11-26 — traffic-analysis-exercise
**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 frames, 3,259.7 sec / ~54 min), `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export)

## 1. Victim host identification

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (confirmed via NBNS name registration and NTLMSSP host field) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString) |
| AD domain / realm | NEMOTODES / NEMOTODES.HEALTH (domain controller **NEMOTODE-DC**, 10.11.26.3) |
| Default gateway | 10.11.26.1 (MAC 00:17:e0:b8:29:5e) |

## 2. Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client).

**Attribution basis: both signature-confirmed and behaviorally confirmed.**
- Signature: ETPRO rules fired directly on the traffic — "ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity", "ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin", and "ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response" (65+ hits against 194.180.191.64).
- Behavioral/protocol confirmation: the HTTP client User-Agent on every C2 request is literally `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, and the request/response bodies use NetSupport's native client32 protocol keywords in cleartext — `CMD=POLL`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1`, and `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>` — sent as HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm`, which is the well-documented NetSupport RAT C2 URI/protocol signature.

## 3. Infection chain (as observed in traffic)

1. `04:49:38 – 04:50:32 UTC` — normal host activity (Windows NCSI check, AD/LDAP/Kerberos traffic, Bing/MSN/Office/Adobe telemetry).
2. `04:50:11 UTC` — DNS query for `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5), immediately followed by:
3. `04:50:14 UTC` — DNS query for **`modandcrackedapk.com`** → resolved to **193.42.38.139**. Suricata flagged this as "ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup" — a known malvertising/cracked-software-lure domain pattern.
4. `04:50:15 – 04:51:20 UTC` — multiple TLS sessions to 193.42.38.139:443 (SNI = modandcrackedapk.com), including one large transfer of **~5.5 MB down** on TCP port 53360 (t=62–67s into capture) — consistent with a fake "cracked APK/software" download page delivering an installer over HTTPS. Content is TLS-encrypted; no plaintext payload or file hash is recoverable from this capture.
5. `04:50:40 UTC` — TLS SNI to modandcrackedapk.com flagged again ("ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in TLS SNI").
6. `04:50:45 UTC` — within ~5 seconds of the large download completing, the host begins beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** using the NetSupport RAT protocol — confirming this download was the malware dropper.
7. `04:50:45 UTC` — one GeoIP self-lookup: `GET /location/loca.asp` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231), response body `33.7488,-84.3877` (Atlanta, GA-area coordinates), used by the RAT to geolocate the compromised host for the C2 panel.
8. `04:50:45 UTC – 05:43:29 UTC` (end of capture) — persistent C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443 continues at a steady ~60-second interval, 58+ HTTP POST checkins observed, spanning the remainder of the capture (~53 minutes) with no sign of termination.
9. `04:49:55` and `04:50:10 UTC` — separate, lower-confidence SMB/EFSR alerts (EfsRpcOpenFileRaw, SMBv1 IPC$ access, NTLMSSP overflow signature) against the domain controller 10.11.26.3 on ports 139/445. These are consistent with routine authenticated Windows domain SMB/RPC traffic (NTLMSSP resolved a NULL/anonymous-looking auth with hostname DESKTOP-B8TQK49) rather than confirmed lateral movement; flagged here for completeness but not attributed to the RAT.

## 4. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — primary NetSupport RAT C2 (HTTP POST `/fakeurl.htm`, plaintext protocol tunneled over port 443, NOT real TLS)

**Malicious / suspicious domains:**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 (malware delivery site, ZPHP-pattern lure domain)
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 (RAT geolocation service, legitimate NetSupport infrastructure abused/used by the malware)
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5 (queried immediately before the modandcrackedapk.com lookup; likely redirector/ad-chain link in the lure)
- `confirmsubscription.com` → 13.56.30.207 / 52.8.34.0 (queried alongside the lure page load; associated with browser push-notification subscription abuse commonly seen on cracked-software sites)

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (C2 checkin/beacon endpoint, POST, repeated 58+ times)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` (GeoIP lookup)
- `https://modandcrackedapk.com/` (TLS-encrypted, exact path not recoverable — payload delivery)

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- No malware binary was recoverable in plaintext from this capture. The dropper transfer at t≈62s (~5.5 MB) occurred entirely inside TLS on port 443 to 193.42.38.139, so tshark's `--export-objects http` could not extract it and **no SHA256 hash can be computed from this evidence**. All HTTP-plaintext objects exported from the capture were benign (Windows CTL/NCSI/OCSP artifacts and the C2's own `fakeurl.htm` protocol responses) — none are the malware executable itself.

## 5. Summary

Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user **oboomwald** (NEMOTODES.HEALTH domain), was compromised after visiting the cracked-software lure site **modandcrackedapk.com** and downloading a ~5.5 MB payload over HTTPS. Within seconds, the host began sustained C2 communication to **194.180.191.64:443** using the **NetSupport RAT** protocol, confirmed both by ETPRO signature hits and by the plaintext `CMD=POLL/ENCD` protocol markers and `NetSupport Manager/1.3` User-Agent. Beaconing was active and ongoing (~60s interval) through the end of the capture, indicating a live, unremediated remote-access compromise at time of capture.
